candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — dynamic postpartum hemorrhage risk stratification and preparedness
candidate.educational_objective: Use postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment as a dynamic care-planning tool by updating risk when clinical factors change and adjusting preparedness before hemorrhage occurs.

options.A: Reassess and update the hemorrhage risk category and adjust anticipatory preparedness and resource planning according to the facility’s protocol.
options.B: Keep the original admission risk category because postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment is completed only once.
options.C: Wait until excessive bleeding occurs before changing the risk classification because risk tools are intended to diagnose hemorrhage after it begins.
options.D: Discontinue ongoing maternal assessment once a standardized risk score has been documented.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance supports stratifying an individual’s postpartum hemorrhage risk and updating that risk as clinical circumstances change, with anticipatory planning for management. A standardized risk tool helps organize preparedness but does not replace ongoing nursing assessment or diagnose hemorrhage after it has already occurred. B incorrectly treats risk as static. C defeats the preventive purpose of risk stratification. D is unsafe because a risk score complements, rather than replaces, continuous clinical assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Postpartum hemorrhage risk stratification should inform anticipatory planning and should be updated as clinical circumstances change; it does not replace ongoing assessment or serve only as a post-hemorrhage diagnostic tool.

candidate.stem: A client was classified as low risk for postpartum hemorrhage on admission to labor and delivery. During labor, new clinical factors increase the client’s hemorrhage risk. Which action should the nurse take?
